newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CANTV to raise tariffs 4.18 pct.
newsitem.headline: CANTV to raise tariffs 4.18 pct.

text.p: Venezuelan national telephone company CANTV will raise its tariffs by an average of 4.18 percent, the company said in a press release.
Late Thursday, both the Ministry of Transport and Communications and Venezuela's National Investment Fund (FIV) said the tariff increase would come into effect April 14.
Both bodies said the increase had been agreed with the understanding that talks with the company on revising the mechanism for calculating tariff rises would continue.

CANTV said international call rates would remain unchanged, as would local long distance rates for calls under 170 kilometers. However, rates for calls that covered distances between 171 and 300 kilometers, 301 to 500 kilometers and over 500 kilometers would be increased five, 10 and 20 percent respectively.

The company said non-residential basic rent for its telephone service would be increased to 9,090 bolivars. Rent for CANTV's three categories of residential user would meanwhile be set at 1,790.86, 2,804.95 and 4,452.86 bolivars.
CANTV said the tariff changes translated into a 10 percent fall in the monthly bill of its average residential client.
